note.headline: Stocks, bonds and credit sell together as crude oil jumps sharply
note.standfirst: Equities, credit and Treasuries all fell in the same session while oil surged, a combination that broke the usual pattern of bonds cushioning stock losses. Positioning built around duration as an equity hedge had nowhere to hide today.
takeaways: Credit sold off across every tier, with investment grade, high yield and EM sovereign debt all closing at session lows alongside equities.
Treasury yields rose in a parallel shift across the curve, so bonds added to the drawdown instead of offsetting it.
Tech dispersion widened sharply: Apple rose +3.56% while Oracle fell -5.38% and Nvidia fell -2.37%.
WTI crude rose +8.27% even as the energy sector fell -0.58%, a clean break between the commodity and the equities that track it.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms broad de-risking, not a single-asset story. The barometer read -1.2, breadth was 6 advancers against 17 decliners, and the largest negative contributors sit in three different asset classes: credit (LQD -2.96), copper (-2.81) and EM debt (EMB -2.41). That spread of pain across credit, commodities and equities is what a genuine risk-off session looks like.

What it contradicts is the standard playbook where Treasuries rally into equity weakness. They didn't. The curve moved in a parallel shift higher, 2-year up 4bp to 4.43%, 10-year up 3bp to 4.83%, and long Treasuries (TLT) closed at a session low alongside investment grade and high yield. The level that decides which read is correct is the 10-year: if it keeps climbing with crude and breakevens, this was an inflation repricing that landed on a risk-off day. If it settles back and credit proxies (LQD, HYG, EMB) find a bid, today reads as a single-session flush.
watching: Whether WTI crude holds its +8.27% gain or gives it back.
Whether the 10-year yield extends past 4.83% or stalls.
Whether LQD, HYG and EMB find a bid after closing at session lows.
Whether the Apple-versus-Oracle/Nvidia split in tech persists or narrows.
note.equities:
Indices fell across the board with growth underperforming value. The Nasdaq 100 fell -1.08%, the Russell 2000 fell -1.04%, the S&P 500 fell -0.59% and the Dow fell -0.60%, the smallest loss among the majors. Mid caps fell -0.94% and the NYSE Composite fell -0.70%, so the damage was not confined to mega caps.

Sector rotation was thin: only staples (+0.05%) and communications (+0.61%) closed higher, the latter carried by Alphabet's +0.59%. Materials (-1.23%) and technology (-1.41%) led the losses, tracking copper's -4.12% drop and a hard split inside big tech. Breadth was 6 advancers to 17 decliners with dispersion at 1.54, among the widest readings in the pack, and single names explain why: Apple rose +3.56% while Oracle fell -5.38%, AMD fell -3.36% and Nvidia fell -2.37%.
note.rates:
Yields rose in a parallel shift across the curve. Two-year up 4bp to 4.43%, five-year up 4bp to 4.61%, ten-year up 3bp to 4.83%, thirty-year up 3bp to 5.28%. The curve itself barely moved: 2s10s flattened 1bp to 40bp, 5s30s flattened 1bp to 67bp, while 3m10y steepened 2bp to 88bp. Tenors from one year out to seven year sit on the session-highs list for yield, and long Treasuries (TLT) and the 7-10 year ETF (IEF) both closed at session lows in price terms.

Breakevens rose alongside nominal yields rather than falling: the 5-year breakeven added 5bp to 2.46, the 10-year added 3bp to 2.40, and the 5y5y forward added 1bp to 2.34. The 10-year real yield also rose 3bp to 2.46, so real rates absorbed only part of the move. No auction result is in today's data.
note.credit: Credit sold off broadly and closed at session lows across the complex. Investment grade (LQD) fell -0.90% to 104.36, high yield fell -0.46% (HYG) and -0.43% (JNK), and EM sovereign debt (EMB) fell -0.81% to 93.41. Leveraged loans (BKLN) were flat at 20.59, the one pocket that didn't participate in the selling. The tone was consistent with the equity move rather than offsetting it, and the extremes list confirms it: EM sovereign USD, US high yield, US investment grade and both Treasury proxies all printed session lows together.
note.fx: The dollar index rose +0.32% to 99.09, but the gain was uneven across G10. USD/JPY rose +0.63% to 154.44 and USD/CHF rose +0.50%, while EUR/USD fell -0.12% and GBP/USD fell -0.25%. AUD/USD was the weakest G10 cross, down -0.84%. In EM, USD/MXN rose +0.43%, USD/BRL rose +0.41%, USD/INR rose +0.65% and USD/TRY rose +0.23% to a session high of 48.575.
note.commodities: Energy led the tape by a wide margin: WTI rose +8.27% to $103.99 and Brent rose +7.85% to $109.15, both far outpacing the -0.58% move in the energy equity sector. Precious and industrial metals moved the other way: gold fell -1.25%, silver fell -5.70%, platinum fell -6.86%, palladium fell -5.51% and copper fell -4.12%. Agricultural markets were mixed but mostly firm, with sugar up +7.50%, corn up +5.07% and soybeans up +2.82%, while coffee fell -9.16%.
note.volatility: The vol surface moved higher across the board. VIX rose +8.38% to 17.84 and VIX9D rose +5.05% to 17.70, while VIX3M fell -3.94% to 19.73, flattening the term structure toward inversion. VVIX rose +8.64% to 102.66 and SKEW fell -1.49% to 147.02. The MOVE index, tracking rate volatility, rose +6.98% to 82.10, consistent with the parallel shift higher in yields.
note.digital: Digital assets sold off in line with risk, not ahead of it. Bitcoin fell -1.51% to $77,075, Ether fell -0.53%, Solana fell -1.72% and XRP fell -2.99%. The moves sit inside the range of the broader equity and credit declines rather than beyond them.
note.international: European indices closed lower across the board ahead of the US session, with the CAC 40 down -1.94%, the SMI down -1.80% and the DAX down -1.66%, the SX5E down -1.58%. Asia was split: the CSI 300 fell -3.60% and the Sensex fell -1.08%, while the KOSPI rose +1.40% and the TAIEX rose +0.17%. The handoff to New York was a market already leaning risk-off before the US open, and US equities extended that tone through the session.
note.correlation:
The defining feature of the session was a positive correlation between equities, credit and rates, all selling off together. That is a break from the pattern where Treasuries provide an offset to equity drawdowns, and it shows up directly in the barometer: LQD, EMB and HYG all rank among the largest negative contributors alongside equity components like RUT and SPX, with MOVE and VIX also contributing negatively.

A second break sits inside commodities. Copper fell -4.12% in a pattern consistent with broader risk-off, but WTI crude rose +8.27% in the same session, decoupling energy prices from the equity reaction to growth risk. If that gap between crude and copper persists, it argues the oil move is being driven by something outside the risk-off narrative that governed the rest of the tape. A convergence back toward copper's read, or a reversal in crude, would be the signal that today's cross-asset correlation was a single-day event rather than a new regime.
